input.reasoning_summary: The claim states that Meta's advertising revenue growth in Q3 2026 was driven MORE by higher average price per ad than by more ad impressions. The evidence clearly supports this claim. E10 and E18 (both with EXACT_MATCH period compatibility and marked as ENTAILS in the evidence review) explicitly state that for the third quarter of 2026, ad impressions increased 10% year-over-year while average price per ad increased 14% year-over-year. Since advertising revenue is the product of impressions and price per ad, and the price increase (14%) exceeded the impressions increase (10%), price mathematically contributed more to the overall 26% advertising revenue growth. In a multiplicative model, the relative contribution can be approximated: price contributed roughly 14/(10+14) ≈ 58% while impressions contributed roughly 10/(10+14) ≈ 42% of the growth drivers. Therefore, price drove more of the growth than impressions, exactly as the claim states. The challenges were refuted: H1 found no explicit statement contradicting the mathematical inference, H2 found no alternative methodology, and H3 confirmed that while mix effects existed, they don't change the fundamental comparison that 14% > 10%.
